The instrument. Not a report card — the point is the pattern: where judgment is consistently sharp versus soft, so the soft spots get drilled until they harden. Mechanism spec: MECHANISM.md.

Two rules. Every rep gets scored, even a bad one. Every skipped week gets a row, so the gap is visible instead of invisible.

The first scored rep — whatever it scores — is the baseline. A measured bad number is worth more than no number, because it is the only thing that makes later improvement visible.

The menu

Pick one a week. The sizes exist so a bad week still produces a scored rep.

Case Company Size Time Exercises
case-01-intel Intel full ~90 min Grove (inflection), Christensen, Helmer, Rumelt, Klarman
case-02-boeing Boeing crux-only ~25 min Goldratt (the constraint), Ohno, Perrow, Bungay
case-03-carvana Carvana single-figure ~10 min Akerlof (lemons), Klarman
case-04-disney Disney full ~90 min Lafley-Martin, Brandenburger-Nalebuff, Schelling, Helmer
case-05-seed-fund-2022 Hypothetical $150M seed fund (June 2022) full, sealed key ~90 min Klarman, Taleb, Tetlock (base rates), Mauboussin; WSS regime map

Each case's "Canon to bring to bear" list is its prime — three to five frameworks, no more. Cases 02–04 deliberately pull canon notes that STRUCTURAL-ANALYSIS.md flagged as never applied.

Recurring gaps — the drill list

From two demo reps only, so a hypothesis rather than a pattern — the mechanism says three before it counts. These are Claude's gaps; whether they are yours is unmeasured.

  • Landscape scored 2 on both. Both memos stayed entirely inside the 10-K: no comparables, no funding or credit-market read, no competitive response. A thesis that depends on an external market — ABS demand for Carvana, certification and supplier capacity for Boeing — cannot be built from the filing alone.
  • A ratio whose construction was never interrogated. Carvana: divided a gross-profit line by a net income produced by a $2.8B tax benefit on a pre-tax loss. Boeing: divided a segment loss substantially composed of reach-forward charges on undelivered aircraft by current-year deliveries. The same error twice — each figure was verified against the filing, but what it was made of was not.
  • Second-order weak exactly where the counter-argument is management's own. Both filings state the opposing case explicitly; neither memo engaged it.
